newsitem.title: GERMANY: West Germany pumps aid into flood-stricken east.
newsitem.headline: West Germany pumps aid into flood-stricken east.

text.p: As unified Germany faces its worst natural catastrophe in its short seven year history, westerners have vowed not to abandon their eastern compatriots to advancing floods, aid organisations said on Monday.

Although weary of bearing the brunt of the costs of rebuilding the run-down former communist east, the flooding has prompted western Germans to open their purses again and offer cash donations, medicine, mattresses and equipment.

"Companies from all over Germany are offering machinery and medicines. Truck convoys from Munich, Hamburg, Cologne are all making their way to the flood area," said Wolfram Eberhardt, a spokesman for the German Red Cross.

"People have rung from all over the country asking: 'What can I do to help?'" he said. "Everyone can identify with such a catastrophe -- with people losing their homes and belongings. The energy of people helping is fantastic."

Some of the worst floods this century in central Europe, which have claimed over 100 lives in Poland and the Czech Republic this month, reached eastern Germany last week as the swollen river Oder burst its banks.

Cyclist Jan Ullrich, Sunday's Tour de France winner, beamed out from the front-page of many western German newspapers, but developments on the banks of the Oder topped most television and radio news bulletins for a second week running.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government, with gaping holes in its budget, record unemployment and weak economic growth already threatening its bid to qualify for Europe's single currency, last week pledged 200 million marks ($108.6 million) in flood aid to the region.
"Thank God Germany has been unified and all Germans regard this as their country and their problem," Kohl said last week while visiting flood-threatened Frankfurt an der Oder.

Interior Minister Manfred Kanther called the flooding, which has forced the evacuation of thousands living by the Oder, a national tragedy and "the worst catastrophe our country has seen for centuries".
During a weekend visit to the region, Kanther remarked that the whole of Germany was meeting on the banks of the Oder, the river which forms part of the German-Polish border.
Thousands of soldiers, border guards, rescue workers and volunteers from all over Germany are toiling day and night to reinforce dikes and prevent further flooding.
Officials said Germans from the western Rheinland, which was hit by severe flooding two years ago, were most sympathetic to the plight of those in the east.
The German Red Cross, which set up one of several special accounts for flood donations, said Germans had given 200,000 marks so far to their "Neighbours in Need" fund.
The Johanniter Accident Aid group said Germans had donated 50,000 marks to their flood fund.
"This is a national task. We helped when there were floods in the Rhine area and now they're helping us," said Wilfried Muder, spokesman for the Brandenberg state government.
